title: Propose mobile-specific layout and navigation improvements
Review project context, existing worklogs, and app structure relevant to current mobile UI
Inspect existing view/navigation components to identify mobile-specific layout opportunities
Synthesize concrete layout and navigation improvement proposals for phone use

content: Starting context review for a UX proposal; no code changes planned unless follow-up implementation is requested.

observation: Structured worklogs should track research tasks and finish/cancel/block all tasks before reporting a proposal.
For any future implementation, prefer simple tested changes and avoid unnecessary complexity; this session is a proposal only unless implementation is requested.

The app is an iPhone-first Expo/React Native MVP with separate connection and session screens, recent hosts/sessions, a host path explorer, live session timeline, collapsible session header, and bottom TUI-like composer.

Recent UI work added keyboard-aware scrolling, bottom-stickiness, collapsed tool accordions, recent host/session history, path explorer, restored resume timeline, TUI-like dark styling, markdown/highlighted tool cards, and compact working indicators. The current gap is not basic mobile support but making navigation/layout feel more native to phones than stacked panels.

The current app is concentrated in one React Native file; ConnectionScreen uses a ScrollView with stacked brand/recent/connect/workspace/path panels, while SessionScreen handles header, FlatList timeline, working indicator, and composer.

content: Context review complete. The app already has a two-screen MVP and phone-minded mechanics; the proposal should focus on stronger mobile information architecture, touch navigation patterns, and reducing stacked configuration panels.
Inspecting App.tsx component boundaries and styles to identify where the UI feels like stacked web panels instead of phone-native navigation.

observation: Connection flow is a linear ScrollView: brand header, recent hosts, recent sessions, connect form, workspace form, and path explorer are all stacked vertically as panels. This makes setup feel like a web form rather than a phone-native flow.

Recent items already contain enough data to become primary navigation surfaces: recent sessions can support one-tap resume/new-here actions, and recent hosts can be a compact horizontal/sectioned picker instead of another vertical panel.

The path explorer is nested at the bottom of the connection screen and renders directory rows in the same column; on phones this should likely become a drill-down picker/sheet with sticky path/actions rather than a subordinate panel.

Session view is closer to a native chat layout: header, timeline FlatList, working row, and bottom composer. The remaining phone-navigation issue is that header actions are small inline buttons and returning to host/setup replaces the session instead of feeling like a modal/drawer.
Composer uses a multiline input plus four wrapped action buttons. On narrow phones, command actions can consume vertical space; a primary send control plus overflow/action bar would feel more mobile.

Navigation state is a simple union of 'connection' and 'session' with no route stack, tabs, drawers, or modal/sheet states. Adding mobile-specific navigation would require new view state or a navigation library.

The mobile app currently does not depend on React Navigation or bottom-sheet/safe-area libraries; proposals should distinguish small custom-state changes from larger dependency-backed navigation patterns.

content: Component inspection complete. The major opportunities are transforming the setup screen into a task-oriented phone flow, promoting recents to navigation, making the path explorer a drill-down sheet, and reducing session header/composer chrome.
Synthesizing a practical proposal with short-term low-risk UI changes and larger navigation improvements for future implementation.

Proposal synthesized around four themes: (1) promote recents and active sessions into the home/dashboard navigation, (2) replace stacked setup panels with progressive drill-down flows and sheets, (3) make the session screen mostly full-height chat with metadata/actions moved to a compact nav bar and overflow sheet, and (4) make composer/tool details thumb-friendly with primary actions visible and secondary controls tucked away.
Proposal complete. No code was changed beyond the structured worklog; next step would be human review and choosing a first implementation slice.
